payload.analysis: Biopsy showing perivascular and interstitial mononuclear infiltrate with innumerable eosinophils and no leukocytoclasia supports an immune/eosinophilic process rather than vasculitis or typical radiation dermatitis. Combined with widespread annular morphology and endometrial cancer history, paraneoplastic/autoimmune eosinophilic dermatosis remains the leading hypothesis. However, direct immunofluorescence, serum autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody panels, and oncology records are still missing, so this cannot be fully confirmed. All currently available key pathology information is covered; further serologic and oncologic correlation is needed.

payload.report: Endometrial adenocarcinoma plus pruritic annular/polycyclic rash and eosinophil-rich infiltrate without vasculitis indicates paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis. Radiation dermatitis and drug/contact hypersensitivity are unlikely given morphology and no new medications/chemotherapy/contrast/travel. Paraneoplastic/autoimmune (node-8), specifically paraneoplastic eosinophilic dermatosis with endometrial adenocarcinoma (node-10), is supported. Missing direct immunofluorescence and autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody tests limit confirmation, but the diagnosis is sufficiently refined.
